title: Power Pages: SDK for native mobile apps and kiosks
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned SDK from existing Power Pages controls and licensing. The documented paths and API calls are supported, and searches found no SDK-specific documentation resolving the stated gaps.

claims.where: What's changing: PWA context
claims.claim: Power Pages already documents enabling a website as a progressive web app.
claims.quote: You can enable your site as a progressive web app (PWA), with native app–like look and feel, by using the Set up workspace in the Power Pages design studio.

claims.where: What's changing: PWA context
claims.claim: The documented PWA mechanism gives a website a native app-like look and feel through browser support.
claims.quote: PWAs are built for cross-platform interoperability through browser support that provides users with a native app–like experience.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: An existing Power Pages site is a website.
claims.quote: Website site settings: These settings apply to specific websites that are associated with the Dataverse environment in which they're being added.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Site settings are under Website > Site settings in the Portal Management app.
claims.quote: Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings with mspp_name, string mspp_value and mspp_websiteid@odata.bind creates the named website site setting.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/mspp_sitesettings; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; mspp_name | Edm.String; mspp_value | Edm.String; mspp_websiteid | mspp_website

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Webapi/<table-name>/enabled has a documented default of False.
claims.quote: Webapi/<table-name>/enabled | Enables or disables the Web API for <table name>. Default: False Valid values: True, False

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Prerequisites and roles
claims.claim: Exposing a table through the portals Web API requires its Webapi/<table-name>/enabled setting to be turned on.
claims.quote: To enable the portals Web API for your site, configure the site settings for each table that you want to expose. ... Confirm that Webapi/<table-name>/enabled is set to True.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Creating only the enabled site setting is not a complete Web API configuration.
claims.quote: This setting is required unless Webapi/<table-name>/UseFieldsFromView is set to True and the configured system view contains at least one eligible column.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Table permissions are under Security > Protect > Table permissions in the Power Pages design studio.
claims.quote: In the design studio on the side menu, select Security. On the left pane in the Protect section, select Table permissions to add and modify table permissions.

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: GET [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/powerpagecomponents reads site components as an inventory operation rather than setting permissions.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/powerpagecomponents; Display name: Site Component; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Site component type 18 denotes Table Permission.
claims.quote: powerpagecomponenttype | Edm.Int32 | Display name: Component Type ... 18 | Table Permission

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A table permission takes effect only when associated with at least one web role.
claims.quote: For a table permission to take effect, it has to be associated to one or more web roles.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The portals Web API follows table permissions granted to users through their associated web role.
claims.quote: The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated web role.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: Table permissions and their web roles provide record-level access control for Dataverse records on existing Power Pages sites.
claims.quote: To allow access to Dataverse records in Power Pages sites, you'll need to configure table permissions and associate the table permissions to web roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The portals Web API is not optimized for third-party services or application integration.
claims.quote: The portals Web API is built for creating a rich user experience inside portal pages. It isn't optimized for third-party services or application integration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages licence.
claims.quote: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Portals Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards anonymous user capacity.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards the anonymous user capacity.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Portals Web API calls by authenticated users require applicable authenticated user capacity licences.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by authenticated users (internal or external) don't count towards page views, but require applicable authenticated user capacity licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages generally uses capacity-based licensing.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages offers authenticated user capacity measured per website per month.
claims.quote: Authenticated users per website/month are calculated as unique users who log into the website in a calendar month duration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages offers anonymous user capacity measured per website per month.
claims.quote: Anonymous users per website/month are calculated as unique users who access one or more anonymous pages of the website in a calendar month duration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages has an authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter measuring actual unique authenticated users per website per month.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of authenticated users who have accessed a website in a month. ... A measure of the number of unique authenticated users per website per month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages has an anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter based on actual unique anonymous website users in a month.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of anonymous users who have accessed a website in a month.
